1.title: Make a loop in the rope
1.say: Hold the long hanging part steady with your left hand. Bring the short loose end over the front of the long hanging part. Let the bottom hang as a round open loop.
placements: short loose end of your rope → laid left to right across front of long hanging part to form one round open loop hanging below the crossing in center of frame in front of you (in the video: blue rope with red flecks outdoors, loose end points left, loop about fist size)
watch_for: If the loop closes or twists, the short end went under instead of over the front. Start again with the end lying flat across the front.
If you see no open circle below, the loop is too small. Make it about fist size so fingers fit through later.
1.check_yourself: It should look like one round open loop with the short loose end lying flat across the long hanging part above the loop.

2.title: Wrap end behind the rope
2.say: Hold the round loop open with your left hand. Bring the short loose end behind the long hanging part and out to the side.
placements: short loose end of your rope → passed behind the long hanging part from front to back and out to the side to make an upper twist just above the lower loop in center of frame (in the video: blue rope with red flecks, loose end sticks out to the right behind the upright part)
watch_for: If the short end stays in front of the long part, you went the wrong way. It must disappear behind then stick out to the side.
If the lower loop disappears, you pulled too far. Keep the lower loop open and round below the twist.
2.check_yourself: It should look like a lower round loop with an upper twist and the short loose end sticking out sideways behind the long part.

3.title: Thread end through loop and tighten
3.say: Push the short loose end down through the lower loop. Pull both ends gently until the eight shape tightens.
placements: short loose end of your rope → pushed down through the opening of the lower round loop from top to bottom in center of frame leaving a short length below (in the video: blue rope with red flecks, end comes out below the knot)

long hanging part above and short loose end below → pulled steadily in opposite directions with both hands until the two stacked loops close into a tight figure eight shape (in the video: snug knot outdoors with upper and lower loops the same size)
watch_for: If the knot looks like a simple oval, the end missed the lower loop. Undo and push the end fully down through the opening.
If the eight shape is loose and floppy, it will slip. Pull both ends again until the crossing is snug.
3.check_yourself: It should look like a tight number eight with two stacked loops and a short end hanging straight below the knot.
